MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  FY 2025-26 BUDGET PUBLIC HEARING AND ADOPTION AND ESTABLISH THE FY
  2025-26 APPROPRIATION LIMIT

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Open the Public Hearing and take any
  public testimony related to the budget adoption, including fees and charges, fund
  balance policy, investment policy, and pension funding policy; 2) Close the Public
  Hearing; and 3) Review and adopt: a. Resolution 2598 - Adopting the
  Consolidated Budget; b. Resolution 2599 - Adopting the City’s Gann Appropriations
  Limit; c. Resolution 2600 - Adopting the Schedule of General Municipal Fees and
  Charges; d. Resolution 2606 - Adopting the Schedule of Community Development
  Department and Public Works Department Fees And Charges; and e. Statement of
  Fund Balance Policy, Statement of Investment Policy, and Statement of Pension
  Funding Policy.

Senior Accountant Estrada provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), summarizing
that there are no major changes to the proposed budget since the City Council Budget Study
Session on June 3, 2024. He highlighted that the City achieved a net-positive result of 5%,
reflecting responsible financial management and contributing to the maintenance of healthy
reserve levels for the City.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, as a member of the Audit/Finance Subcommittee alongside
MAYOR STEGURA, commended staff on their work on the budget.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, to open the public hearing.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN explained what the GANN Limit is for the benefit of the public,
noting that Rolling Hills Estates is under the limit by $16,000,000.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JUNE 24, 2025

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 250169
  AMENDMENT AND RESTATEMENT OF CHAPTER 17.56 OF THE CITY OF
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO ACCESSORY
  DWELLING UNITS
  LOCATION: CITYWIDE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JUNE 24, 2025
   Recommendation: That the City Council continue the public hearing on the
  amendments to Chapter 17.56 to the July 22, 2025 City Council meeting.

Community Development and Public Works Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per
the agenda material), noting that after issuing the public hearing notice for this item, staff
received correspondence regarding the proposed revisions, and requires additional time to
address the comments and potential additional revisions to the proposed amendments. Staff
recommends continuing the item for City Council review and consideration to the July 22, 2025
City Council meeting.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  CONTINUE THE PUBLIC HEARING ON THE AMENDMENTS TO CHAPTER
  17.56 TO THE JULY 22, 2025 CITY COUNCIL MEETING.

There being no objection, MAYOR STEGURA so ordered.

C.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 250169

Community Development and Public Works Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 753 by title.

B.  OVERVIEW OF CITY EMERGENCY OPERATIONS PLAN

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file this report and the City’s
  Emergency Operations Plan.

Assistant to the City Manager Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Consultants from Risk Management Professionals Ryan Bray and Shireen Kulkarni provided
a presentation showing the basic plan outline and functional annexes of the Emergency
Operations Plan (EOP).

Consultant Bray explained how scalable Incident Comments Systems (ICS) can be, which can
even be completed by one single person, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JUNE 24, 2025
 He also noted that if there are multijurisdictional efforts, ICS can be expanded to be more
complex and fit into larger arenas.

Discussion ensued about how the EOP and the Hazard Mitigation Plan function together, and
that the EOP is a changing/living document that will evolve with the City’s needs over time.

City Manager Grammer noted that the City’s response to the Peartree Lane Land Movement
in July 2023 helped inform the contents of the Emergency Operations Plan.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  RECEIVE AND FILE THIS REPORT AND THE CITY’S EMERGENCY
  OPERATIONS PLAN.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

C.  TASK ORDER FOR MICHAEL BAKER INTERNATIONAL, INC., TO PREPARE A
  SUPPLEMENTAL EIR AND A MASTER PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
  WITH COTTON SHIRES & ASSOCIATES TO PERFORM PEER REVIEW OF
  GEOTECHNICAL INFORMATION FOR THE BRICKWALK RESIDENCES PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Authorize the City Manager to enter into
  a Task Order with Michael Baker International, Inc., to prepare a Supplemental EIR
  for the Brickwalk Residences Project, in a not-to-exceed amount of $485,512,
  approved as to form, by the City Attorney; and 2) Authorize the City Manager to enter
  into a Master Professional Services Agreement with Cotton Shires & Associates to
  perform third party peer review of geotechnical information, in a not-to-exceed
  amount of $78,775 for the Brickwalk Residences Project, subject to approval as to
  form, by the City Attorney.

Senior Planner Whitney Berry provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Senior Planner Berry explained that the selection of the consultants is under the City’s
purview, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

Community Development and Public Works Director Naughton explained that these units
will apply to the City’s Regional Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA) requirements, but not
until building permits are issued, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN assured the community that the City Council will perform
its due diligence in reviewing the project to ensure it is appropriate for the City.

MAYOR STEGURA emphasized there will be many opportunities for public comment over
the next year and a half, stated that it is wise of staff to look for a peer review of the
geotechnical information by Cotton Shires, and noted that the applicant is bearing the cost
of the environmental reports.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received by Lisa Geisel and Valarie Anderson who expressed concerns
about the project.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ highlighted the many ways in which the community can stay
informed about this project, including the “interested parties list”, Commission and City Council
agendas, meetings and minutes, as well as signing up for e-notifications on the City’s website.

MAYOR STEGURA explained the City’s RHNA requirements and State Density Bonus Law.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
JUNE 24, 2025
   COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  MICHAEL BAKER INTERNATIONAL, INC., TO PREPARE A SUPPLEMENTAL
  EIR FOR THE BRICKWALK RESIDENCES PROJECT, IN A NOT-TO-EXCEED
  AMOUNT OF $485,512, APPROVED AS TO FORM, BY THE CITY
  ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

With it being her last City Council meeting with the City, Senior Planner Berry thanked the

D.  SECOND AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT WITH BENNETT LANDSCAPE FOR
  LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE SERVICES

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Second Amendment to the
  Agreement for chemical-free Landscape Maintenance Services with Bennett

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ commended Bennett Landscaping for their work with the City.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER echoed COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ’s sentiments,
specifically commending Bennett’s weed abatement efforts.
